title: The Evening Brief: FOMC begins; whale flows turn onto exchanges
dek: The Federal Reserve's two-day policy meeting opens today as the main event of the week. Underneath, the desk's Whale Watch board shows a third consecutive week of large asset movements onto exchanges, while stablecoin inflows suggest positioning shifts ahead of the FOMC conclusion.
author: GoCheckMyCrypto
key_fact: The FOMC meeting (October 27-28) is the week's primary checkpoint; markets are pricing in rate expectations while whales accumulate on-exchange, and stablecoin buying power is moving off exchanges, a pattern that typically precedes volatility.
bottom_line: The FOMC meeting dominates Tuesday's calendar, with the two-day session concluding tomorrow. Whale behavior shows a third consecutive week of asset inflows onto exchanges, paired with net stablecoin withdrawals, suggesting traders are positioning ahead of the rate decision. Per the desk's boards, Bitcoin funding remains warm at 0.01% 8-hour on OKX, long-to-short ratios remain bullish, and spot Bitcoin ETFs took in $110.3 million on the day, October 26, offsetting weekly outflows of $115.2 million. Watch the FOMC announcement tomorrow for any shift in market positioning.
body: The Federal Open Market Committee's two-day meeting began today and concludes tomorrow, making it the focal event of the week. Bitcoin is up 1.35% over 24 hours; per the desk's boards, bitcoin trades at $80,809 with fear and greed at a neutral reading of 48. Broader price action is subdued: Bitcoin down 2.25% over seven days and down 5.20% over thirty days; Ether up 1.87% over 24 hours but down 3.54% over seven days and down 13.91% over thirty days.

Whale behavior on the desk's Whale Watch board shows sustained inflows onto exchanges over three consecutive weeks. The week ending October 27 recorded $691 million net moving onto exchanges, continuing the pattern from October 13 ($1,557 million onto exchanges) and October 20 ($772 million onto exchanges). Within that, Ethereum saw the largest single move: $370,030,906 net moving onto exchanges over the past seven days, with $420,356,490 in inflows and $50,325,584 in outflows. Bitcoin contributed $293,414,862 net onto exchanges. On the stablecoin side, the desk's Whale Watch board shows $121,467,832 net moving off exchanges over the same window, indicating traders are withdrawing stablecoin buying power from venues, a posture typically adopted ahead of anticipated volatility.

Spot Bitcoin ETF flows diverged by window: spot Bitcoin ETFs took in $110.3 million on the day, October 26, but saw net outflows of $115.2 million over the week through October 26. Ethereum spot ETFs saw net inflows of $4.5 million on October 27, though the last five sessions through that date recorded net outflows of $175.4 million.

Funding rates remain warm across major venues. Per the desk's boards, bitcoin 8-hour funding on OKX sits at 0.01%, annualizing to 11.0%. Ethereum 8-hour funding is 0.0086% (9.4% annualized). Long-to-short ratios remain skewed toward longs: bitcoin at 2.1:1, Ethereum at 2.27:1, and Solana at 3.02:1, suggesting sustained bullish positioning despite the week's subdued price moves.

The calendar ahead narrows to one event: the FOMC meeting concludes tomorrow, October 28, with a policy announcement expected. Bitcoin difficulty is estimated to adjust upward 5.37% when the retarget occurs at 260 blocks to go. No regulatory deadlines are imminent per the desk's tracking.
